issues.legal_issue: A retrenchment carried out after a transferee has taken over an undertaking and become the workers’ employer is not retrenchment consequent upon the transfer.
material_facts: The transferee took possession of the undertaking before the workmen were retrenched, and the required approval for the transfer had been obtained before the retrenchment.
The transferee controlled and supervised the work, paid the workers’ wages, and made operational decisions concerning the undertaking.
The retrenchment notices were issued after the transferee had become the employer of the workmen.
issues.conclusion: The transferee was the employer when the retrenchment occurred, so the retrenchment was not consequent upon the transfer and section 25FF did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25FF concerns retrenchment consequent upon a transfer of ownership or management. Where the transfer has already taken place and the transferee has become the employer, a later retrenchment is governed by the ordinary retrenchment provisions, not section 25FF. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.industrial_dispute_over_retrenchment: The proceeding concerned a dispute over the termination of industrial workers’ employment.
predicates.transfer_control_passed_before_dismissal: Operational control of the undertaking passed to the transferee before the workers were dismissed.
predicates.transferee_controlled_work_and_paid_work: The transferee directed and supervised the workers’ work and paid their wages.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns a retrenchment after control has passed to a transferee that directed the work and paid the workers, the transferee is treated as their employer and the dismissal is not treated as consequent on the transfer.

issues.legal_issue: A retrenchment is invalid when the employer fails to satisfy the statutory preconditions and procedure for retrenchment.
material_facts: The retrenchment was treated as having been effected by the transferee, which had become the employer.
The transferee had not complied with the requirements of section 25F or section 25G.
No reasons had been recorded for departing from the ordinary order of retrenchment under section 25G.
issues.conclusion: The retrenchment was invalid because the employer had not complied with section 25F or section 25G.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25F prescribes conditions precedent to retrenchment, including notice to the workman, compensation, and notice to the appropriate Government. Section 25G prescribes the procedure for retrenchment, ordinarily requiring the last person employed in a category to be retrenched first unless reasons for choosing another workman are recorded. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.industrial_dispute_over_retrenchment: The proceeding concerned a dispute over the termination of industrial workers’ employment.
predicates.employer_retrenched_workers: The employer brought the workers’ employment to an end as a retrenchment.
predicates.employer_did_not_satisfy_retrenchment_pr: The employer did not satisfy all required preconditions for retrenchment.
predicates.employer_departed_from_ordinary_retrench: The employer did not follow the ordinary order for selecting workers for retrenchment and recorded no reasons for that departure.

issues.definition: In a dispute over retrenchment, if the employer fails to satisfy the required preconditions and departs from the ordinary selection order without recording reasons, the retrenchment is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: An employer may retrench workers only for proper industrial reasons supported by a genuine need to reduce the workforce.
material_facts: The transferee directed that the eight workers be treated as surplus and their services terminated.
No case was made out that the workers had become surplus in the undertaking or that a proper industrial or trade reason justified their retrenchment.
issues.conclusion: The retrenchment was not justified because no proper reason for retrenching the workmen had been established.
issues.legal_principle: Although management ordinarily determines the workforce needed to run an undertaking, industrial adjudication may examine whether a disputed retrenchment was justified. Retrenchment may be justified where workers become surplus because of rationalisation, economy reasonably and bona fide adopted, or other industrial or trade reasons. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.industrial_dispute_over_retrenchment: The proceeding concerned a dispute over the termination of industrial workers’ employment.
predicates.employer_sought_to_reduce_workforce: The employer sought to reduce the number of workers in the undertaking.
predicates.no_surplus_or_valid_business_reason_show: The employer did not establish that the workers were surplus or that a genuine industrial or trade reason justified the reduction.

issues.definition: If an employer seeks to reduce its workforce and establishes neither that workers are surplus nor another valid business reason, the retrenchment is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: Acceptance of retrenchment compensation does not bar workers from challenging the validity of their retrenchment in industrial adjudication.
material_facts: The eight workers accepted retrenchment compensation paid by the outgoing management.
The workers’ union protested the next day, and the workers claimed they had been compelled to accept the compensation and had done so without prejudice to their challenge.
issues.conclusion: The workers’ acceptance of compensation did not bar them from challenging the retrenchment.
issues.legal_principle: Technical pleas of waiver or similar bar are not generally entertained in industrial adjudication; in the circumstances, receipt of compensation did not prevent the workers from contesting the retrenchment. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.industrial_adjudication_challenge: The proceeding was an industrial adjudication in which workers challenged their retrenchment.
predicates.workers_accepted_retrenchment_compensati: The workers received compensation paid in connection with their retrenchment.
predicates.workers_promptly_protested_or_claimed_co: The workers promptly protested the retrenchment or claimed that they had been compelled to accept the compensation.

issues.definition: In an industrial adjudication, when workers who received retrenchment compensation promptly protest or claim compulsion, their acceptance does not bar their challenge.

issues.legal_issue: An invalid retrenchment does not terminate the employment relationship and entitles the workers to reinstatement with continuity of service and back wages, subject to adjustment for compensation received.
material_facts: The transferee was the employer when the workers were retrenched.
The retrenchment was invalid for noncompliance with the applicable requirements and because no proper justification had been established.
The workers had received retrenchment compensation.
issues.conclusion: The workers remained employees and were entitled to reinstatement with continuity of service and full back wages from retrenchment until reinstatement, with appropriate adjustment for compensation received.
issues.legal_principle: An invalid retrenchment does not terminate the employer–employee relationship. The workers are entitled to reinstatement, continuity of service, and back wages, with compensation already received taken into account. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.industrial_dispute_over_retrenchment: The proceeding concerned a dispute over the termination of industrial workers’ employment.
predicates.employment_relationship_was_not_terminat: No valid dismissal terminated the employment relationship between the employer and the workers.

issues.definition: When an invalid retrenchment in an industrial dispute has not validly terminated employment, the workers are entitled to reinstatement, continuity, and back wages, with compensation received taken into account.
